summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour discusses the parameters and permissibility of transmitting religious knowledge, particularly focusing on three categories: that which is definitively from Allah and His Messenger (obligatory to spread), that which is definitively not from Allah (forbidden to spread), and that which might be from Allah (permissible but not obligatory). He emphasizes the importance of accurate transmission of hadith and warns against spreading unverified narrations, especially in the age of social media. Sh. Ali Mashhour uses the example of stories from the People of the Book, explaining that while certain narratives may be permissible to mention, Muslims should not actively seek knowledge from non-Islamic sources or use them to interpret the Quran. He stresses that spreading any narration attributed to the Prophet without scholarly authentication is prohibited.
